references.text: The Lord God sends Adam and Eve out of the Garden of Eden and into the wilderness, which can be seen as a parallel to Jesus being led out into the wilderness.
Satan quotes this psalm to justify tempting Jesus, which directly links these verses to the event in Matthew 4:1.
Isaiah's prophecy about one who would bear our sicknesses and sorrows can be viewed in light of Jesus' sufferings and temptations in the wilderness.
John the Baptist's ministry in the wilderness prepares the way for Jesus, who himself goes out into the wilderness to be tempted.
Luke's account of Jesus' temptation in the wilderness provides a parallel event and offers further details about the temptations.
Hebrews speaks of Jesus as a high priest who can sympathize with our weaknesses, since he himself has been tempted in every way.
